triage_notes: Does AVX-512 exceed 1.4x the AVX2 FMA peak? Measured zmm 93.59 GFLOP/s (8 accs) vs ymm 50.84 GFLOP/s (8 accs) = ratio 1.841 — YES (> 1.4 threshold)(29.2 vs 15.9 flops/cycle at the measured 3.20 GHz). The ymm probe reproduces machine.json's basis once normalized by clock: 50.84 GFLOP/s at a measured 3.20 GHz TSC = 15.9 flops/cycle, vs machine.json's 57.62 at its 3.566 GHz core-clock estimate = 16.2 flops/cycle (2 FMA ports x 8 flops/ymm-FMA); same micro-architectural rate, the absolute gap is host clock variation on this shared KVM vCPU. The 16-accumulator zmm variant measures 103.92 GFLOP/s vs 93.59 with the task-prescribed 8 accs, so the 8-acc zmm number understates the zmm FMA peak; the ratio below uses the 8-acc number as specified. Roofline recomputation with measured numbers: p*_avx512 = 8*93.59/21.39 - 1 = 34.01 (vs p*_avx2 = 18.01 this run; machine.json said 23.4 with 57.62/18.89 — within this host's known run-to-run DRAM and clock variance; anchoring the zmm peak to machine.json's committed 18.89 GB/s gives p*_avx512 = 38.64, so p* lands in the 34-39 band regardless of DRAM anchor). The q=8 DRAM kernel's bound stays 2.99-3.39 ns/row (64 B/row / 21.39-18.89 GB/s) — the DRAM path is unchanged by ISA, and the shipped v3 kernel already sits at 17.4% (19.7% at the machine.json anchor) of it with a load-port ceiling per ADR-0012 (~1.15 ymm-load-uops/cy). The q=32/q=65 cache-case bounds with the zmm peak would become 11.28/45.84 ns/row (vs 20.77/84.39 at the ymm peak); holding v3's measured ns/row fixed (i.e. NO rewrite, only the roof moves), the hypothetical % of bound DROPS to 22.4% (q=32) and 30.0% (q=65) from 41.2%/55.2% — a faster FMA roof makes an unchanged kernel look WORSE against it; H6's >= 70% of FMA peak in cache becomes HARDER to reach with an AVX-512 roof unless the kernel itself is rewritten to zmm. VERDICT: NOT-WORTH. Reasoning from the measurements: the shipped kernel sizes that matter (q=8/q=17, DRAM-resident) are bound by loads/DRAM, not FLOP rate (ADR-0012: v1->v3->v4 moved 2%->22%->20% of bound; the ceiling is load-port throughput). A zmm FMA-peak gain of 1.84x does not move the DRAM bytes/row or the load-port floor. The load-path measurement (the only AVX-512 lever that could move G2 per ADR-0012's re-open condition: 64 B loads halving the load count) shows L1 load bandwidth 146.0 GB/s with zmm 64 B loads vs 118.8 GB/s with ymm 32 B loads (1.23x) — 64 B loads do NOT move materially more bytes per load-uop on this host, so even the load-path re-open condition is not met. This probe measured the FMA peak and DRAM bandwidth; the FMA-side verdict is NOT-WORTH, and the load-side re-open condition (ADR-0012: 32 B loads halving the load count) remains the honest trigger for any AVX-512 build. CV flags: fma_ymm 4.6%, dram_2t 6.3% (> 3% per asm-benchmarking §2; shared-KVM jitter, medians stable).
